name: NY-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+32 partisan lean makes the seat structurally out of reach for Republicans
Brad Lander has raised $2.45 million while Jennifer Moore has raised $2,693, an overwhelming resource gap
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at 98 percent
Open seat with no general-election polls or expert ratings limits precision
model.rationale: A D+32 New York City seat, a fundraising gap of nearly a thousand to one favoring Lander, and 98 percent market pricing leave the Republican nominee without a plausible path; the Democratic primary was effectively the decisive contest.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for the Republican or a sharply worse national environment for Democrats could trim the margin, though not the likely outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dan Goldman (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
New York's 10th District is a heavily Democratic New York City seat with a partisan lean of D+32, and Democrats hold it. Incumbent Dan Goldman lost renomination, so the general election is an open-seat contest, but the Democratic nominee, Brad Lander, enters as a heavy favorite after raising $2.45 million. Republican Jennifer Moore has reported just $2,693 raised and $1,526 on hand, with no outside spending on either side.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the stark money gap, and market pricing: Polymarket puts Democratic chances at 98 percent. The expected margin is roughly 33 points, with moderate uncertainty given the lack of polling. The primary was effectively the decisive contest; the general election is not competitive on the current evidence.
